article_title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a post-Putin future

tasks.prompt: What change among some Russian tycoons does the article identify?
options: They have openly formed a party to remove Putin immediately
They are quietly considering how to regain influence or achieve healthier politics after Putin
They have abandoned all interest in Russian politics
They have collectively transferred their wealth to the government
tasks.correct_answer: They are quietly considering how to regain influence or achieve healthier politics after Putin
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מתארת כיצד חלק מהעשירים מתחילים לדמיין את היום שאחרי פוטין — מחזרת אוליגרכיה ועד פוליטיקה פתוחה ובריאה יותר.

tasks.prompt: How has the Kremlin used a “carrot and stick” policy toward wealthy businessmen since 2022?
options: It offered every critic a government ministry
It seized critics' assets while rewarding loyalists with war contracts
It ended sanctions and returned every yacht
It required all billionaires to leave Russia
tasks.correct_answer: It seized critics' assets while rewarding loyalists with war contracts
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ה'מקל' היה תפיסת נכסים של מבקרי המלחמה, וה'גזר' היה חוזים ממשלתיים נדיבים לנאמנים.

tasks.prompt: What three broad post-Putin paths do analysts discuss?
options: Democracy, renewed autocracy, or a return to oligarchic rule
Monarchy, military occupation, or division into states
Immediate EU membership, neutrality, or isolation
Communism, colonialism, or direct corporate ownership
tasks.correct_answer: Democracy, renewed autocracy, or a return to oligarchic rule
tasks.explanation_hebrew: התרחישים הם פתיחה דמוקרטית, ממשיך אוטוקרטי חדש, או חזרה למערכת אוליגרכית בסגנון שנות התשעים.

tasks.prompt: What does “jockey for position” mean in the discussion of wealthy Russians with liquid cash?
options: Compete strategically to gain influence or advantage
Move their money into horse racing
Leave politics to security officials
Publicly donate all their assets
tasks.correct_answer: Compete strategically to gain influence or advantage
tasks.explanation_hebrew: jockey for position פירושו להתחרות ולמקם את עצמך אסטרטגית לקראת מאבק עתידי על כוח והשפעה.

tasks.prompt: Why was Andrey Melnichenko's interview with The Economist considered unusual?
options: He announced that he would become prime minister
He admitted to owning no businesses
A very rich Russian spoke to a publication from a country the Kremlin views as unfriendly and argued against one-man rule
He revealed the date of Putin's departure
tasks.correct_answer: A very rich Russian spoke to a publication from a country the Kremlin views as unfriendly and argued against one-man rule
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הראיון היה חריג משום שאוליגרך בכיר דיבר עם כתב עת ממדינה לא ידידותית וקרא לשינוי שיסיים שלטון של אדם אחד.

tasks.prompt: What does it mean that Putin “subjugated” the oligarchs after taking power?
options: He placed them under his control and reduced their independent power
He gave them equal authority over the state
He encouraged them to fund opposition parties
He allowed them to write the constitution
tasks.correct_answer: He placed them under his control and reduced their independent power
tasks.explanation_hebrew: subjugated פירושו הכפיף אותם למרותו וצמצם את כוחם העצמאי להשפיע על הפוליטיקה.

tasks.prompt: Why do analysts regard a democratic transition as the least likely immediate outcome after Putin?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשר בין מצב המוסדות, תרבות האלימות וקשיי המעבר.
expected_points: Democratic institutions have been eroded or destroyed during Putin's rule
Russia has become accustomed to repression and violence
Standard democratic procedures are no longer familiar or well established
A power vacuum could favour organised elites or another authoritarian figure
Building functioning democratic competition would take time

tasks.prompt: Summarise how Putin changed the position of oligarchs and why some are now thinking about a post-Putin order.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשוות בין שנות התשעים לעידן פוטין, ולשלב מלחמה, סנקציות ותמריצים כלכליים.
expected_points: In the 1990s, wealthy businessmen used money to influence politicians
Putin brought them under state control after 2000
The Khodorkovsky case warned them about the cost of opposition
Since 2022 critics have lost assets while loyalists received state contracts
Western sanctions limit their lives and business abroad
Some now feel politically powerless and see the war as a dead end
They hope eventually to regain influence or see more open politics

tasks.prompt: Why might tycoons with liquid cash behave differently from those dependent on state contracts?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר כיצד מבנה העושר משנה את מידת החופש והסיכון הפוליטי.
expected_points: Liquid cash is less directly dependent on continued government favour
Financially independent tycoons may feel safer building alliances or preparing for succession
Those reliant on state contracts can lose their wealth if the Kremlin turns against them
Dependence therefore discourages political manoeuvring
Even independent tycoons still face serious personal risk under Putin

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced paragraph assessing whether an oligarchic revival could produce a healthier post-Putin Russia.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג אפשרות לפתיחות לצד סיכוני שלטון האליטות, ולהשתמש ברקע ההיסטורי מהכתבה.
expected_points: Some tycoons want less repression, freer speech and stronger political competition
A weaker successor might create space for pluralism
The 1990s oligarchic system involved corruption, cronyism and elite control of politicians
Rule by a few wealthy clans would not itself be democracy
A healthier outcome would require institutions and public accountability, not only redistributed elite power
